drug_identity.name_en: Saline Cathartics (Magnesium Citrate, Hydroxide, Oxide, Sulfate; Sodium Sulfate)
drug_identity.active_ingredient: Magnesium Citrate, Magnesium Hydroxide, Magnesium Oxide, Magnesium Sulfate, Sodium Sulfate
drug_identity.reversal_evidence: Calcium has been suggested to help antagonize the CNS effects of magnesium during an overdose.
drug_identity.off_label_note: Saline cathartic products are not FDA-approved for use in veterinary species. All dosages listed are extra-label.

metabolism_and_clearance.extra_information: Up to 30% of an orally administered dose of magnesium salts can be absorbed. Concurrent furosemide may be used to enhance the renal excretion of excess magnesium during an overdose.

organ_burden_logic.note: Based on precautions, contraindications, and overdose effects.

brain.evidence: Hypermagnesemia (from chronic use or overdose) may manifest as CNS depression.

blood.evidence: Electrolyte disturbances are possible. Use with extreme caution in patients with electrolyte abnormalities.

kidney.evidence: Use with extreme caution in patients with renal insufficiency.

heart.evidence: Sodium-containing laxatives are contraindicated in patients with congestive heart failure. Use with extreme caution in cardiac disease. Hypermagnesemia can cause ECG changes.

brain.evidence: Hypermagnesemia may manifest as CNS depression.

kidney.evidence: Use with extreme caution in patients with renal insufficiency.

heart.evidence: Contraindicated in CHF (sodium sulfate); extreme caution in cardiac disease.

timing_profile.evidence: Up to 30% of an orally administered dose of magnesium salts can be absorbed. Onset of action in monogastric animals is typically 3 to 12 hours.

_ddi_note: May alter the rate and extent of absorption of other orally administered drugs by shortening intestinal transit times.

drug_interactions.evidence: Increased risk for quinidine toxicity. Also listed as having reduced oral bioavailability if administered with magnesium-containing cathartics (separate by 2 hours).

drug_interactions.drug: Oral Drugs (e.g., Fluoroquinolones, Digoxin, Tetracyclines, Ketoconazole, Iron, Sucralfate)
drug_interactions.evidence: May have reduced oral bioavailability if administered with magnesium-containing cathartics; separate dosages by at least 2 hours.

dosage_list.context: Cathartic to enhance toxin removal (Magnesium hydroxide)
dosage_list.duration_note: Rarely used as a laxative but recommended for zinc phosphide ingestions.

dosage_list.context: Cathartic to enhance toxin removal (Magnesium sulfate or Sodium sulfate)
dosage_list.duration_note: Administered as a suspension in water up to 20%. May be combined with activated charcoal. If repeated AC doses are needed, cathartic should only be given with the initial dose.

dosage_list.context: Cathartic to enhance toxin removal (Magnesium hydroxide)
dosage_list.duration_note: Rarely used as a laxative but recommended for zinc phosphide ingestions.

dosage_list.context: Cathartic to enhance toxin removal (Magnesium sulfate or Sodium sulfate)
dosage_list.duration_note: Administered as a suspension in water up to 20%. May be combined with activated charcoal.

renal_dose_adjustment.note: Use with extreme caution in patients with renal insufficiency.

effects_and_mechanisms.common_mechanism: Hyperosmotic effect of poorly absorbed magnesium cations causes water retention, stimulates stretch receptors, and enhances peristalsis. Shortens transit times and increases cholecystokinin release.

species_notes.dog: Sodium sulfate is typically preferred to magnesium sulfate in small animal species. Rarely recommended for treating constipation in small animals, but used for toxin removal.
species_notes.cat: Sodium sulfate is typically preferred to magnesium sulfate in small animal species.

dog.evidence: Contraindicated in dehydration and long-term use. Sodium sulfate contraindicated in CHF or congenital megacolon. Extreme caution with renal insufficiency, water imbalance, electrolyte abnormalities, cardiac disease, or severe depression.

cat.evidence: Contraindicated in dehydration and long-term use. Sodium sulfate contraindicated in CHF or congenital megacolon. Extreme caution with renal insufficiency, water imbalance, electrolyte abnormalities, cardiac disease, or severe depression.

storage_and_forms.storage: Store milk of magnesia at temperatures less than 35°C (95°F), but do not freeze.

section_1_2_10.highlights: Hyperosmotic agents used for constipation or to increase elimination of GI toxins. Contraindications include dehydration and long-term use. Sodium sulfate contraindicated in CHF or congenital megacolon. Adverse effects include cramping and nausea. Hypermagnesemia can occur with chronic use.
section_1_2_10.indications: Relieve constipation or shorten intestinal transit time to reduce absorption of orally ingested toxicants. In small animals, rarely recommended for constipation but used to enhance toxin removal.
section_1_2_10.client_info: Give as directed by your veterinarian. Contact your veterinarian if your animal begins vomiting.
